items.title: 삼성바이오에피스, 글로벌 제약사와 자가면역질환 치료제 美서 판매

items.title: 심텍, 영업익 4년 만에 1000억원 돌파

items.title: 동진쎄미켐, 中 디스플레이 소재 사업 '엑시트'

items.title: Temperature-Independent Logarithmic Current Slope in Interdiffusion-Broadened Silicon pn Junction toward Low-Power Thermometry
items.abstract: With the development of cryogenic technologies such as quantum computing, there is an increasing need for low-power cryogenic thermometers that minimize self-heating. Here, we report an anomalous temperature-independent logarithmic current slope, $d(\ln J)/dV$, in heavily doped silicon p$^{+}$n$^{+}$ junctions with significant dopant interdiffusion and highlight the advantages of our device as a low-power, cryogenic thermometer. Electrical characterizations from 2 to 420 K reveal that, at low forward bias, $d(\ln J)/dV$ remains nearly constant, which yields a voltage-temperature responsivity that is nearly independent of bias current. The observed transport cannot be fully understood with conventional diffusion or direct band-to-band tunneling. Instead, the results suggest the contribution of trap-assisted tunneling. These results establish interdiffusion-broadened silicon p$^{+}$n$^{+}$...

items.abstract: The spin splitting of an altermagnet arises from a rotation that relates its two magnetic sublattices. In known cases it is fixed by the crystal structure. Here we show that guest-host frameworks separate the two roles. In the boron-carbon clathrates $M$B$_3$C$_3$ the ordered cage removes the translation between the two guest sites and enforces cubic $i$-wave altermagnetism, with six symmetry-enforced nodal planes, for any magnetic guest in the compensated state; strain retunes the class to $d$- or $g$-wave. items.snippet: 지난 30일 오후 서울 지하철 2호선 역삼역 사거리는 직장인들로 붐볐다. 하지만 역 출구에 있는 구두 수선대는 한적했다. 수선대 앞을 오가는 직장인 대부분은 운동화를 신고 있었다. 25년째 이곳에서 구두를 닦아온 이상훈(66)씨는 “10여 년 전만 해도 하루 30~40켤레씩 닦았는데 요즘은 손님이 2~3명뿐”이라며 “구두만 닦아서는 먹고살 수 없어 오후 4시 30분이면 문을 닫고 밤마다 배달을 뛴다”고 했다.

items.title: 한국 6000만원 VS 미국 200억원
items.snippet: 2022년 12월 A씨는 전북 정읍시 한 국도에서 자전거를 끌고 걸어가다 시속 93㎞로 달리던 차량에 부딪혀 숨졌다. 이 도로의 제한 속도는 시속 60㎞였다. 법원은 작년 6월 사고 운전자에게 “위자료 총 6500만원을 유족에게 지급하라”고 판결했다. 재판부는 “운전자가 과속하지 않았다면 경미한 충격만 가했을 것”이라면서도 “야간에 야광 조끼 등 안전장치 없이 보행한 A씨에게도 일부 책임이 있다”고 했다.

items.title: “대통령, 대법관 후보 선정 개입은 안되고 대법원장도 대통령 판단 제한하면 안돼”
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 대법관 재(再)제청 논란과 관련해 헌법재판소에 의견서를 제출한 것으로 2일 확인됐다. 이 대통령 측은 의견서에서 “대통령의 임명권은 제청된 후보자를 임명하지 않을 권한을 포함한다” “대통령이 새 후보자 제청을 요청하는 것은 임명권의 본질이자 핵심”이라는 주장을 폈다. 장동혁 대표 등 국민의힘 의원 109명은 지난 9월 “이 대통령의 대법관 후보자 임명 동의안 미제출과 재제청 요구로 국회의 대법관 임명 동의권과 국회의원의 심의·표결권이 침해됐다”며 헌재에 권한쟁의심판을 청구했다. 이에 이 대통령 측은 21쪽 분량의 답변서를 지난달 13일 헌재에 제출했다.

items.title: 판사 80% “재판 중 AI 가짜판례 경험”
items.snippet: 현직 판사 10명 중 8명이 재판 과정에서 인공지능(AI)이 만든 가짜 판례가 담긴 서면을 받아본 적이 있는 것으로 2일 나타났다. 법원행정처가 지난달 각급 법원 법관 360명을 대상으로 실시한 AI 관련 설문 조사 결과다. 대법원이 공개한 조사 결과를 보면, 민사·가사·행정 담당 법관 중 약 80%가 잘못된 판례를 적용하거나 아예 없는 판례를 가짜로 만들어 인용한 사례를 경험했다고 답했다. 변호인 선임 비율이 높은 형사 담당 법관 등을 포함해 전체 응답자 중에선 67.5%가 이 같이 답했다. 유형별로는(복수 응답) 존재하지 않는 판례를 인용한 경우가 80.7%로 가장 많았고, 엉뚱한 판례를 인용한 경우 65.4%, 가짜 법령 인용 16.9% 등이 뒤를 이었다. 논문 등 AI가 만든 가짜 자료를 인용한 경우도 4.1%로 조사됐다.

items.title: 안전의 역설… 하청 챙길수록 ‘사용자’로 판정
items.snippet: 국내 건설사 현대엔지니어링은 올 6월 중앙노동위원회로부터 노란봉투법상 하청업체의 ‘진짜 사장’(사용자성)에 해당되는 만큼 하청 노조 요구대로 교섭에 응해야 한다는 통보를 받았다. 현대엔지니어링은 현행 산업안전보건법(산안법)에 따라 산업안전보건관리비를 책정하고 하청업체가 사용 계획을 제출하면 그 비용을 지급·감독하는 내용을 하청업체와의 계약서에 명시해 놓고 있었다. 또 현장 안전 관리 차원에서 안전 수칙을 위반한 하청 노동자를 작업에서 퇴출하는 제도를 운영하고, 일일 안전 회의를 진행해 왔다. 대부분 산안법상 의무를 이행하기 위한 안전 조치였지만, 중노위는 이를 사용자성 판단 근거로 삼았다.

items.title: [신문은 선생님] [사소한 역사] 비싼 설탕 대신 옥수수로 만든 ‘단맛’… 당분·열량 섭취 쉬워 비만 위험 커요
items.snippet: 의사들이 비만을 초래한다고 경고하는 대표적인 성분이 바로 액상과당입니다. 크림이 잔뜩 들어간 디저트, 지방이 가득한 음식과 달리, 액상과당은 주로 음료수에 들어 있어 시원하고 빠르게 섭취할 수 있어요. 하지만 액상과당이 들어 있는 달콤한 음료를 자주 마시면 당분과 열량을 지나치게 섭취하기 쉬워 비만 위험이 커질 수 있어요.

items.title: [신문은 선생님] [뉴스 고사성어] 다양한 요구 빗발친 프랑스 시위와 ‘중구난방’의 숨은 뜻
items.snippet: 무리 중(衆) 입 구(口) 어려울 난(難) 막을 방(防) 프랑스가 시위로 몸살을 앓고 있습니다. 학생들이 학습 환경 개선을 요구하며 시작했는데, 다양한 이가 참가한 후 폭력으로 번져 상점 약탈과 방화도 잇따르고 있어요. 교육 여건 개선, 물가와 연료비 인하, 복지 예산 요구, 공무원 임금 동결 반대까지 사회 각계의 목소리가 뒤섞인 상황입니다. 여러 분야에서 각기 제 주장을 하느라 통제가 어려운 상황이 됐습니다. 이럴 때 어울리는 말이 ‘뭇사람의 입은 막기 어렵다’는 뜻의 중구난방입니다. 중구난방의 현재 뜻은 여럿이 저마다 떠들어 갈피를 잡기 어려운 상황을 가리키지만, 본래는 여론은 억누른다고 사라지지 않는다는 뜻이었습니다.

items.title: [신문은 선생님] [재미있는 과학] 에스컬레이터 한 줄 서기, 편마모가 기계 고장 부추겨요
items.snippet: 빼빼로 과자를 주고받는 날로 널리 알려진 11월 11일. 사실 이날은 ‘승강기 안전의 날’이기도 합니다. 승강기는 엘리베이터와 에스컬레이터 등 동력을 사용해 사람이나 화물을 위아래로 나르는 장치를 말하는데요. 행정안전부와 한국승강기안전공단은 매년 기념식을 열고, 안전한 승강기 사용에 대한 홍보를 합니다. 또 영상, 포스터 등 공모전을 진행하는데, 에스컬레이터에서 뛰거나 걷지 말자는 내용이 많이 담깁니다. 그런데 과연 우리는 에스컬레이터를 얼마나 안전하게 이용하고 있는 걸까요? 지하철역에서 에스컬레이터를 타다 보면 익숙한 풍경이 눈에 들어와요. 오른쪽에는 사람들이 빽빽하게 서 있고, 왼쪽은 바쁜 사람들을 위해 비워두고 있죠. 이를 ‘한 줄 서기’라고 해요. 그런데 과연 한 줄로 서고 다른 줄을 비워두는 게 미덕일까요? 아니면 양쪽에 나란히 서는...

items.title: “포퓰리즘 버리고 국익 택한 獨 총리들… 우리도 과감한 결단 내릴 지도자 절실”
items.snippet: 김황식 전 총리와 독일의 인연은 각별하다. 서른 살이던 1978년 마르부르크 대학교에서 1년간 독일 민법을 배웠고, 총리로 퇴임한 2013년 다시 베를린자유대학으로 건너가 독일의 정치와 법 제도를 공부했다. 그의 40년 공직 생활의 화두는 ‘독일’. “같은 분단 국가였는데 독일과 한반도의 오늘은 왜 다를까?”를 파고든 그는 ‘독일의 힘, 독일의 총리들’이란 책으로 그 해법을 제시하기도 했다.

items.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. VII. Step kinetics
items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate the kinetics of attachment of new segments of the crystalline lattice (pyramids) at steps on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs(-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb(-1-1-1) surfaces. Diffusion species are gallium adatoms at high coverage or gallium adatoms connected with nonmetal atom creating stable pyramids. These pyramids arrive at the steps, and cannot be attached be directly because the Ga adatom at the pyramid base cannot be attached directly. Therefore they are incorporated into the step by additional nonmetal atoms glue atoms arriving from the vapor or detached from other segments of the surface terraces.

items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate surface diffusion of adsorbates on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs (-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb (-1-1-1) surfaces. The mixed coverage consists of Ga adatoms in the first layer with a nonmetal atom attached above them forming a triangular-based pyramid. The pyramidal structures are stable during surface jumps involving rotations around one of the basal Ga adatoms. Thus, the diffusion proceeds via rotation (pivot) of the pair of the other basal Ga adatoms around an immobile Ga adatom moving them into new, originally empty sites. items.title: Cross-Domain Joint-Embedding Pretraining For Heterogeneous Industrial Time Series
items.abstract: Industrial predictive maintenance and manufacturing tasks frequently contain abundant sensor measurements, but with limited labeled data. We investigate cross-domain self-supervised pretraining using joint-embedding predictive architecture for heterogeneous industrial time series (JEPA-HITS), which learns one encoder from various domains such as battery, semiconductor chemical mechanical planarization (CMP), computer numerical control (CNC) machining, and bearing while preserving dataset-specific temporal scales. We evaluate representation reuse on regression and classification problems under reduced-label downstream training, and leave-one-domain-out (LODO) pretraining. items.title: Gate-tunable superconductor-semiconductor coupling and its impact on zero-energy modes in PbTe-Pb nanowires
items.abstract: Superconductor-semiconductor coupling in hybrid nanowires plays a pivotal role in Majorana devices. Here, we demonstrate this tunable coupling in PbTe-Pb nanowires and its impact on the induced gap and zero-bias peaks (ZBPs). In the strong coupling regime, the device reveals a clean superconducting gap, where robust and non-robust ZBPs are observed in distinct magnetic field ranges. Conversely, increasing the gate voltage drives the system toward the weak coupling regime, where the gap becomes narrow and soft. Consequently, robust ZBPs disappear while non-robust ones persist. Our results establish a direct link between tunable coupling and robust ZBPs, providing guidelines on engineering Majorana zero modes and topological qubits.

items.title: Amplification of valley polarization in an hBN-separated MoSe2-WSe2 heterostructure
items.abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenide heterostructures host long-lived interlayer excitons in the +K and -K valleys that can encode long-lived valley polarization. We investigated the low-temperature valley polarization dynamics in an MoSe2-bilayer hBN-WSe2 heterostructure. The bilayer hBN spacer results in an interlayer exciton lifetime exceeding 2 μs and an anomalous valley polarization amplification effect. Our theoretical model shows that this amplification results from the long exciton lifetime and exciton-exciton interactions. This work sets the stage for long-lived interlayer excitons to be used in nonlinear valleytronic transistors and amplifiers.

items.title: Optical Detection of Coefficient of Thermal Expansion via Frequency Tracking at Cryogenic Temperatures
items.abstract: Accurate characterization of the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) in nanoscale thin films is critical for predicting residual stress and ensuring the reliability of modern micro-electromechanical systems and advanced semiconductor architectures. The primary limitation is that traditional methods depend on precise thickness measurements or are restricted to crystalline materials. In this work, we present an in-situ, non-destructive optical methodology to determine the CTE of suspended nanofilms by tracking the temperature-dependence of their vibrational frequency. This approach eliminates thickness measurements entirely and works for amorphous films where X-ray diffraction (XRD) fails. We experimentally validate this technique across a broad temperature range, evaluating membranes in their native microstructure state without requiring additional destructive patterning or complex sam...

items.title: Band Alignment of Grafted versus Directly Bonded Si/Ge Heterostructures
items.abstract: The electronic properties of semiconductor heterostructures are influenced by the local bonding and electrostatic environment at the heterointerface. Here, we investigate how the interface-formation mechanism modifies the band alignment of Si/Ge heterostructures by directly comparing Al2O3-mediated semiconductor grafting with direct bonding. Interface-sensitive X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy combined with Kraut analysis reveals type-I band alignment for both structures, but with different band offsets: the valence-band offset increases from ~0.08 eV for directly bonded Si/Ge to ~0.21 eV for grafted Si/Al2O3/Ge, accompanied by a corresponding reduction in the conduction-band offset. Raman spectroscopy further distinguishes the two interfacial configurations. items.title: Nondestructive 3D Metrology of Through-Glass Via Geometry and Internal Wall Texture Using Holotomography
items.abstract: Through-glass vias (TGVs) are increasingly important for semiconductor packaging, yet their internal geometry and wall texture remain difficult to characterize nondestructively. Here, we use holotomography (HT) to inspect the three-dimensional (3D) geometry and internal wall texture of intact, unfilled TGVs before metallization. HT reconstructs the refractive index (RI) distribution of the glass and via. Maps of RI and spatially filtered RI then localize the internal boundary. Geometric fitting quantifies via dimensions and taper, while spatial filtering separates slowly varying wall form from finer texture. The reconstructed surface supports volumetric visualization, dimensional measurements and spatial characterization of wall texture within one optical inspection workflow. These measurements reveal internal features inaccessible from surface views and provide quantitative descriptors...

items.title: Trapping photo-carriers in undoped gate-defined quantum dots using an on-chip microwave resonator for charge readout
items.abstract: Scaling up gate-defined quantum dot systems is hindered by the rapid growth in the number of control gates. To tackle this challenge, we propose a different approach where the quantum dots are created from optically generated charges trapped beneath accumulation gates. By shining an above-the-gap laser light onto an undoped GaAs substrate, we demonstrate that it is possible to create and separate electron-hole pairs to form quantum dots. For the charge readout, we use a superconducting coplanar waveguide resonator capacitively coupled to the quantum dots. With these elements, we demonstrate a working many-charge double quantum dot device comprised of only two plunger gates, one tunnel coupling gate and one sensing gate. items.abstract: Silicon Photo-Multipliers (SiPMs) are semiconductor-based photodetectors that offer performance comparable to that of traditional Photo-Multiplier Tubes (PMTs), while providing several advantages, including low operating voltage, immunity to magnetic fields, compact size, and mechanical robustness. These features have led to their widespread adoption in scintillator-based detectors for both fundamental and applied physics. In recent years, there has been a growing interest in the detection of scintillation light at cryogenic temperatures in low-temperature experiments based on bolometric detectors, such as RES-NOVA and CUPID, as well as in emerging quantum applications. In the RES-NOVA experiment, radiopure PbWO$_4$ crystals are used to detect supernova neutrinos. items.abstract: As demand for semiconductor talent grows, education must prepare learners for the complexity of modern chip design. Instruction typically relies on lectures, textbooks, software exercises, and limited laboratory experiences. Although foundational, these approaches offer limited support for understanding the spatial, multi-scale, and interconnected nature of chip design. Virtual reality (VR) can help learners visualize and interact with complex structures and processes, but its educational opportunities remain underexplored. We examined this gap through chip design curriculum analysis and semi-structured interviews with five participants representing instructional and learner perspectives. We characterized four learning demands: descriptive knowledge, procedural knowledge, relational and design-focused reasoning, and strategic decision-making. items.title: Visualizing Anisotropic Charge Transport in CrSBr using Bias-Dependent Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
items.abstract: Anisotropic semiconductors offer unique opportunities for next-generation electronics due to their direction-dependent transport. However, conventional electrical measurements provide only spatially averaged characteristics. Here, we employ bias-dependent Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) to directly visualize the response of CrSBr under different electrical bias configurations. Spatially resolved KPFM maps reveal highly distinct, crystallographic-direction-dependent potential profiles. To elucidate this behavior, we employ anisotropic transport simulations that capture the charge transport and electric-field distributions in CrSBr. The close agreement between experiment and simulation provides a unified picture of anisotropic charge transport and bias-induced potential redistribution. items.title: A Mixed-Precision CNN-LSTM Accelerator Featuring Long-Kernel Memory Reuse and Dynamic Quantization for Sleep Staging
items.abstract: This letter presents a mixed-precision CNN-LSTM accelerator for EEG-based sleep staging. To efficiently execute long temporal convolutions, a serpentine dataflow propagates activations between neighboring processing elements, reducing memory accesses by 6.2 times and 2.25 times compared with output- and weight-stationary dataflows, respectively. A hybrid quantization scheme applies runtime dynamic quantization to the LSTM and MLP layers and assigns mixed precision on a layer-by-layer basis, reducing model size by 4.16 times. Combined with a bit-flexible MAC architecture and channel-grouped memory scheduling, the accelerator supports INT2/4/8/16 inference. Fabricated in 65 nm CMOS, the accelerator consumes 0.40 mW and achieves a 258 times speedup over an iso-frequency 32b RISC-V processor. items.title: Field-resolved observation and quantification of the instantaneous Kerr response in semiconductors
items.abstract: The optical Kerr effect, whereby the refractive index of a material changes with light intensity, underpins nonlinear photonics and emerging mid-infrared technologies. Accurate determination of the nonlinear refractive index is therefore essential, yet conventional intensity-based techniques infer the nonlinear phase shift indirectly from changes in beam propagation or optical spectra. Moreover, methods such as the $z$-scan cannot resolve the temporal evolution of the nonlinear response, making it difficult to distinguish instantaneous Kerr nonlinearities from delayed contributions, including free-carrier effects. Here, we investigate the nonlinear optical response of germanium at $5 μ\mathrm{m}$ using field-resolved degenerate pump-probe spectroscopy. items.title: Full-Potential Korringa Kohn Rostoker Study of Structural and Mechanical Properties in SiGeSn Alloys
items.abstract: Accurate first-principles descriptions of open, covalently bonded crystal structures remain challenging within conventional Korringa--Kohn--Rostoker (KKR) approaches owing to the spherical approximations commonly employed for the effective crystal potential. Here, we systematically assess the recently developed full-potential KKR (KKR-FP) implementation in the open-source MuST package and demonstrate its applicability to diamond-structured group-IV semiconductors and SiGeSn alloys. Benchmark calculations for diamond-structured Si reveal substantial limitations of the conventional muffin-tin and atomic sphere approximations, whereas KKR-FP accurately reproduces the experimental equilibrium lattice parameter and bulk modulus, yielding 5.433 and 94.9 GPa. items.title: Dipolar Exciton Polarons in a van der Waals Homobilayer
items.abstract: Fermi polarons exemplify how many-body interactions give rise to emergent quasiparticles, providing a fundamental framework for understanding interacting quantum matter. In electron-doped two-dimensional semiconductors, exciton polarons offer optical access to Fermi-polaron physics and electrical tunability, yet achieving stronger and more controllable exciton-electron interactions remains a key challenge. Here, we realize dipolar exciton polarons in an electrically tunable van der Waals homobilayer, where interlayer excitons with spatially separated electrons and holes act as quantum impurities carrying permanent electric dipole moments. These dipolar polarons exhibit substantially enhanced exciton-electron interactions, with binding energies more than four times those of conventional intralayer exciton polarons. We further demonstrate that Fermi-sea layer polarization provides an addit...

items.title: Photonic Crystal Integrated Graphene-Silicon Schottky Diodes for Resonant Infrared Photodetection
items.abstract: Narrowband infrared (IR) photodetection has become a critical technology for the next generation of smart low-power photodetectors. In this work, we present a device based on a graphene-silicon Schottky junction with narrowband response in the short-wave IR (SWIR) regime. Integrating a photonic crystal (PhC) slab in the device enables a wavelength dependant tailoring of graphene absorption. The devices were characterized by photocurrent measurement, which was enhanced more than two orders of magnitude by the PhC integration. The sharp enhancements obtained can also be predicted by numerical simulation. This approach offers a highly scalable, tunable, CMOS-compatible architecture for narrowband IR photodetection, paving the way for next-generation, low-power IR sensors.

In the current batch, single-photon detection is achievable at 400 eV with an SNR > 5, while the QE surpasses 85 % at 250 eV. Combined with the high frame rates of CMOS readout ASIC, iLGAD sensors make the hybrid pixel detectors excellent candidates for time-resolved magnetic Small Angle X-ray Scattering (mSAXS) experiments in the soft X-ray energy range. In this contribution, we evaluated ILGAD sensors bump-bonded to 25 μm pitch charge-integrating MÖNCH chips at a laser-driven soft X-ray source. items.title: Y2CdX4 (X = S, Se, Te) Semiconductors: A First-Principles Study of Structural, Electronic, Optical, and Energy-Related Properties
items.abstract: We present a comprehensive density functional theory (DFT) investigation of the structural, mechanical, electronic, optical, thermoelectric, and bonding properties of Y2CdX4 (X = S, Se, Te) compounds for potential optoelectronic and energy-conversion applications. Structural optimization reveals a systematic expansion of the equilibrium lattice parameters from S to Te. The calculated bulk moduli decrease from 83 GPa for Y2CdS4 to 68 GPa for Y2CdSe4 and 54 GPa for Y2CdTe4, indicating progressive lattice softening. Electronic band-structure calculations predict indirect band gaps of 2.42, 2.08, and 1.71 eV for Y2CdS4, Y2CdSe4, and Y2CdTe4, respectively, with further narrowing upon inclusion of spin-orbit coupling. items.abstract: Colloidal semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) are highly promising materials for various applications, yet photoluminescence intermittency (blinking) remains a key obstacle to their practical use. While recent advances have enabled partial or complete suppression of this effect, both the degree of suppression and the mechanism by which it occurs are often difficult to establish. In the present work we analyse the blinking suppression of single CdSe/ZnS QDs after treatment with p-phenylenediamine (PPD), recently discovered by Yang et al. We revisit the blinking mechanism in this system and show that it is governed predominantly by the trapping mechanism, rather than by Auger ionization as previously proposed. items.abstract: Electron-phonon interactions in materials with free carriers are dynamically screened by low-energy electronic excitations, yet first-principles calculations almost always treat this screening in the adiabatic approximation. items.abstract: Au-free ohmic contacts and refractory gate stacks are critical for integrating ultra-wide-bandgap (UWBG) Al-rich AlGaN transistors with Si-CMOS technology. In this work, we demonstrate, to our knowledge, the first complete Au-free metallization platform for Al$_{0.65}$Ga$_{0.35}$N-channel MOS-HEMTs, combining electron-beam-evaporated and sputtered Ti/Al/Ti ohmic contacts with sputtered TiN and Pt gate metals. The Ti/Al/Ti contacts achieved a contact resistance of approximately 7.5--7.7 $Ω\cdot$mm while being fully Au-free. This contact resistance is achieved using a 600 $^\circ$C anneal, substantially below the 850--950 $^\circ$C typically required for Au-capped Ti/Al/X/Au contacts on Al-rich AlGaN, indicating a reduced thermal budget and improved compatibility with silicon-CMOS foundries. items.title: Efficient Simulation of Gate Leakage Currents in Ultra-scaled Transistors from First Principles
items.abstract: To ensure high electrostatic integrity in ultra-scaled field-effect transistors (FETs), thin gate dielectric layers are typically needed, potentially giving rise to (strong) leakage currents. Being able to model this effect is therefore crucial. Here, we show how gate leakage currents can be computed at the ab initio level in WS$_2$-hBN FETs by extending the well-established quantum transmitting boundary method (QTBM). Two main challenges are tackled: (i) the calculation of the open boundary conditions (OBCs) for the gate contacts and (ii) the solution of the resulting sparse linear system of equations A x = b where the matrix A possesses an unstructured sparsity pattern. We demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the state of the art and can be readily applied to simulate transistors with gate lengths exceeding 25 nm.

items.title: Electric field control of anisotropic spin traffic between spin-filtering and magnon-scattering in a layered antiferromagnet
items.abstract: Layered A-type antiferromagnetic (AFM) semiconductors offer a unique platform for spintronic devices by combining robust magnetism with gate-tunable semiconducting properties. We present a dual-gate field-effect transistor based on CrSBr, a layered A-type AFM with pronounced transport anisotropy and complex spin dynamics. Our device provides independent control over carrier density and displacement field. Systematic transport measurements reveal that the displacement field, rather than doping, predominantly governs the sign and magnitude of magnetoresistance ratio (MRR). We identify the origins of both negative and positive MRR components and connect them to interlayer and intralayer spin-dependent transport mechanisms. items.title: Uncertainty-aware Feedback Loop Diagnosis: integrating reinforcement learning and conformal prediction for reliable wafer defect classification
items.abstract: Semiconductor manufacturing is a complex, multi-step process that requires both high precision and low operating costs. Therefore, detecting defects in a high-volume setting is an important component of wafer map analysis for reliable production. However, most state-of-the-art deep learning approaches require a full scan of the surface, which hinders the development of high-throughput inspection systems. items.title: Electronic liquid crystals and superconductivity from doping a moiré Mott insulator
items.abstract: Electronic liquid crystals, such as stripe phases and nematics, are self-organized states of matter with spontaneously broken rotational symmetry. They are expected to emerge in a doped Mott insulator as a compromise between short- and long-range Coulomb interactions, and are believed to be intimately connected to the emergence of high temperature superconductivity either as a competing order or an intertwined order. Moiré semiconductors provide a controllable platform to explore the relationship between stripe phases and superconductivity near a Mott insulator. items.abstract: Constructing accurate and physically interpretable tight binding (TB) Hamiltonians from first principles calculations remains challenging, particularly for materials exhibiting complex orbital hybridization, spin orbit coupling (SOC), and magnetic order. SKFitter is an open-source Python framework for constructing and optimizing symmetry resolved Slater Koster TB models directly from density functional theory (DFT) calculations performed using Quantum ESPRESSO or VASP. The framework supports s to f orbitals, incorporates on site SOC and site resolved magnetic exchange interactions, and accommodates both orthogonal and nonorthogonal basis. items.title: PDE-based Bayesian Inverse Problems in All-at-once Framework
items.abstract: We propose a modern all-at-once framework for PDE-based Bayesian inversion by introducing the PDE residual as probabilistic information. In this framework, the PDE residual is treated as a soft constraint with a residual covariance and is directly incorporated into the likelihood function. The new hybrid likelihood function eliminates PDE solves, thus reducing expensive computational costs, while performing rigorous Bayesian inference. Theoretically, we establish the well-posedness of the posterior with uncertainty quantification, and numerically, we propose two efficiency inversion algorithms based on two posterior sampling methods. items.title: OPERA: OPamp Design by an Expert-Taught Reasoning Agent, from Specifications to Layout
items.abstract: Analog flows from specifications to a signed-off layout rarely run without manual iteration. Recent large language model (LLM) agents size circuits with optimizer loops over the device dimensions and stop at the schematic. We present OPERA (OPamp design by an Expert-taught Reasoning Agent), in which a general-purpose LLM agent designs CMOS opamps from specifications to post-layout sign-off with open-source tools. First, the designer teaches the agent the gm/ID method: map the specifications to transconductances and minimum currents, choose gm/ID per device role from characterized lookup tables, and size from equations, leaving a few knobs to search and an explainable design. Second, the agent learns the gLayout framework and taught layout practice, and writes a reusable layout generator that closes the layout and extraction loop at designer-approved gates. items.title: Characterizing Performance Tradeoffs in Heterogeneous GPU-Wafer-Scale Accelerator Systems
items.abstract: As AI accelerator architectures become increasingly diverse, integrating different architectures into a unified system is emerging as a new heterogeneous computing paradigm. GPUs and WSEs differ substantially in compute, memory, and communication organization, creating both architectural complementarity and additional overheads, yet how to translate this heterogeneity into practical performance gains remains unclear. To address this gap, we propose a hierarchical benchmarking methodology to characterize GPU--WSE heterogeneous execution and the conditions for exploiting complementarity, together with an analytical performance model that identifies when heterogeneity becomes a bottleneck and when it yields system-level performance gains.

items.title: Colossal magnetoresistance in narrow-gap magnetic semiconductor Eu$_2$CdAs$_2$
items.abstract: Discovering antiferromagnetic materials with a sizable colossal magnetoresistance (CMR) effect and precisely tuning their responses remain significant challenges in materials science. This work reports the synthesis, phase transitions, and magnetotransport properties of the narrow-gap Zintl arsenide Eu$_2$CdAs$_2$. The compound undergoes antiferromagnetic ordering at $T_\mathrm{N} = 9$ K and exhibits semiconducting behavior with a low-temperature activation energy of 3.2 meV, achieving a large CMR effect of $-10^4\%$ at 9 T. Below $T_\mathrm{N}$, a distinct butterfly-shaped magnetoresistance hysteresis emerges without any macroscopic ferromagnetic order, revealing a transport anomaly likely dictated by AFM domain dynamics and/or the formation and percolation of localized magnetic polarons. items.title: Lone-Pair Stereoactivity Overrides Mass Scaling of Thermal Expansion and Heat Conduction in Non-vander Waals Layered Bismuth Oxychalcogenides
items.abstract: Heavier chalcogens are generally expected to soften isostructural semiconductor lattices, raising thermal expansion and lowering thermal conductivity. Layered bismuth oxychalcogenides, Bi2O2X (X = S, Se, Te), are mixed-anion crystals whose covalent slabs and ionic sheets are bound electrostatically rather than by van der Waals forces and whose Bi3+ 6s^2 lone pairs can become stereochemically active. Despite the rapid development of Bi2O2Se for fin and gate-all-around transistors, its fundamental thermal expansion and heat transport mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we show that lone-pair stereoactivity, not chalcogen mass, governs both properties. items.title: Numerical schemes for 1D capacitively coupled plasma fluid simulation
items.abstract: Capacitively coupled plasmas (CCP) are widely used in semiconductor manufacturing, where fluid models provide an efficient approach to the simulation of the low-temperature discharge. The model considered in this work couples the electron and the ion continuity equations, the electron energy equation and the Poisson's equation for the electric potential. We investigate the numerical schemes for the simulation of the 1D-CCP. In particular, a semi-implicit Scharfetter-Gummel (SG) scheme is adopted for the Poisson's equation, while the remaining equations are solved using the implicit SG schemes. The proposed strategy can be naturally extended to the 2D cases. Several alternative schemes are also discussed and tested. Numerical experiments compare these methods in terms of the admissible time step $Δt$, total simulation time, accuracy against a reference solution and robustness of the schem...

items.title: Volumetric Nanophotonics for Enhanced Scintillation and Remote Light Outcoupling
items.abstract: Nanophotonic patterning is a promising approach to enhancing light extraction in scintillator materials, with the potential to improve performance in applications such as medical imaging and particle detection. While 2D surface patterns have been successful in improving scintillator performance, the true potential of nanophotonic patterning lies in the bulk, where photons are emitted, transported, and absorbed. Here, we experimentally demonstrate the enhancement and control of scintillation using 2.5D volumetric nanophotonic patterns. Using a direct femtosecond laser writing approach, we nanofabricate square lattices of air holes into the bulk of inorganic scintillators (YAG:Ce and YAG:Yb), achieving nearly subwavelength periods compared to the peak emission wavelength and depths up to hundreds of microns, which fill a large fraction of the full thickness of the bulk. items.title: A Case Study of a Multi-Agent Kernel-Optimization Loop That Learns a New AI Accelerator
items.abstract: Frontier large language models write correct CUDA kernels for most single-operator benchmark tasks, yet their accuracy collapses on accelerators whose architecture and programming language they have rarely seen. We present a case study of an LLM agent loop built for such accelerators. Our example is the FuriosaAI RNGD NPU, programmed in a recent, sparsely documented Rust DSL, where the loop optimized three Gemma-4-12B decode kernels over 12 days on a shared, scarce device. The loop builds its own target knowledge: it writes and checks a summary of the DSL documentation, measures the chip with microbenchmarks, records compiler-derived legality rules, and revisits this knowledge when the toolchain changes, rechecking rules and measurements where it can. items.abstract: Design-based metrology of academic electron beam lithography (EBL) is bottlenecked by low-throughput imaging. For integrated photonics, where nanometre-scale structural variation can significantly limit device performance, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is the standard tool for critical dimension (CD) metrology, revealing the structure of devices that is not available from optical measurements. Manual SEM imaging on a wafer-scale is time-intensive, can feature operator-dependent distortions, and yields too few data to reliably close the nanofabrication calibration loop. The following details a methodology that utilises existing hardware in an academic cleanroom: a GDSII-to-SEM software workflow that converts a facility's superseded pattern generator into a CD-SEM for unattended image acquisition and efficient CD and line edge roughness (LER) extraction. items.title: Coherent control and high purity single-photon emission from telecom quantum dots on metamorphic InGaAs
items.abstract: Semiconductor quantum dots emitting in the telecommunication O- and C-bands are promising candidates as single-photon sources for fiber-based quantum communication. In this work, we show how coherent quasi-resonant and phonon-assisted excitation help reveal the intrinsic optical properties of InAs quantum dots embedded in relaxed InGaAs matrices on top of metamorphic InGaAs layers for achieving emission in the telecom bands. By systematically comparing excitation schemes, we separate excitation-induced effects from intrinsic emitter properties. This allows us to observe linewidths as narrow as 21 $μ$eV, the disappearance of slow decay channels, and single-photon purity reaching second-order autocorrelation values in the order of $10^{-2}$. items.title: Parity-Resolved Many-Body Kinetics of a Topological Qubit under Nonequilibrium Phonon Pulses
items.abstract: Phonon bursts from ionizing radiation cause correlated errors in superconducting quantum processors. We study prescribed nonequilibrium phonon pulses in a Majorana qubit formed by two $2\,μ\mathrm{m}$ proximitized nanowires. Combining the lattice Lutchyn--Oreg model, microscopic electron--phonon coupling, and parity-resolved many-body dynamics, we track excitation, relaxation, and logical coherence. Without quasiparticle escape, recombination restores the initial Majorana occupations in about 130 ns, while phonons exchanged during excitation and recovery can retain logical-state information, leaving permanent coherence loss. For mirror-symmetric wires, the fractional coherence loss per wire is 0.75--1.0 times the excitation probability averaged over the two logical states, even at zero Majorana splitting; breaking mirror symmetry can suppress dephasing at small splitting. items.abstract: Digital SRAM compute-in-memory (CIM) macros enable energy-efficient CNN inference by eliminating off-chip weight transfers; however, peripheral control logic introduces three inefficiencies: bit- slice over-activation at reduced precision (L1), unnecessary accumula- tion depth (L2), and idle precision-transition stalls (L3). To address these, we present four synthesizable peripheral blocks: a Flush-Merge Enable (FME) controller, a Confidence-Based Early-Exit (EE) module, a Precision Register with Decoder (PR/PD), and a Bit-Serial Cycle Controller (CC), co-designed to minimize switching activity, wordline overhead, and leakage. Implemented in TSMC 65-nm CMOS at 335 MHz, the peripheral framework occupies 1769.760 μm2 post-synthesis and 1982.131 μm2 post-PnR. items.title: A Fast and Memory-Efficient Algorithm for Searching Faint Moving Objects using Synthetic Tracking
items.abstract: Detecting unknown faint moving objects using optical imaging is challenging. Long exposure times are infeasible for such targets, as the resulting image streaking causes a loss of signal-to-noise ratio due to energy dispersal across multiple pixels. To address this, synthetic tracking, a track-before-detect method, replaces long exposures with many short exposures, integrating them in post-processing to recover the moving signal. Enabled by modern CMOS detectors with fast readout and low read noise, this technique synthesizes telescope tracking by searching over a grid of velocities. However, the conventional brute-force implementation imposes a significant computational burden: integrating N_f frames of size (N_x,N_y) requires O(N_x N_y N_f^3) operations. This cost becomes prohibitive for megapixel-scale frames with N_f~100. Although dynamic programming can reduce the computational comp...

items.title: Back-End-Of-Line Integration of 2-Terminal Ferroelectric Hafnia Synaptic Weights on Commercial CMOS Process
items.abstract: Functionalising the back-end-of-line (BEOL) of CMOS with emerging materials is a key route to neural network accelerators and neuromorphic systems. In this work, we demonstrate for the first time the integration of 2-terminal ferroelectric synaptic weights in the BEOL of as-delivered commercial 180 nm CMOS dies. A novel material stack is proposed, in which a WOx/[HfO2-ZrO2] bilayer is sandwiched between TiN and Mo electrodes. For devices annealed at 450 °C, programming below 1.8 V is achieved with a cycle-to-cycle variation below 3 %. Synaptic weights annealed at 500 °C exhibit more gradual weight updates, while the tested underlying NMOS transistors remain functional after the complete integration process. The trade-off between thermal budget and on-device training performance is illustrated using hardware-aware neural network simulations.

items.abstract: Scientific reasoning in specialized engineering fields depends on knowledge scattered across the literature, often proprietary and absent from frontier LLM training data. items.abstract: Spintronic terahertz (THz) emitters based on ferromagnet/heavy-metal bilayers provide an efficient route for generating broadband THz radiation through ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion. However, Ni/Pt bilayers usually exhibit relatively weak THz emission, limiting their use as efficient spintronic emitters. The enhanced emission reverses polarity with the magnetic field and follows the expected angular dependence of ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion. items.title: Machine Learning Hamiltonians with Polarizations for Heterogeneous Systems
items.abstract: Machine learning Hamiltonians use local atomic structures to determine local Hamiltonian matrix elements without carrying out self-consistent calculations. They have been used to study large systems and to carry out high-throughput screening for their electronic and optical properties. The prediction of the Hamiltonian is essentially the prediction of the electron electrostatic potential energy; however, for heterogeneous systems, this potential energy is often determined by faraway features, such as interface or surface dipoles, or even an applied voltage in a nanodevice. Thus, it cannot be determined by local atomic structures alone. items.abstract: In this work, a recessed-gate Ga-polar AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) on sapphire incorporating an AlGaN back-barrier for W-band operation is demonstrated. The device achieves a subthreshold slope of ~130 mV/dec, a peak transconductance of 0.75 S/mm, and an fmax exceeding 240 GHz. Continuous-wave load-pull measurements at 94 GHz show an output power of 3.75 W/mm with a power-added efficiency of 31.8%. This performance significantly exceeds the best previously reported Ga-polar devices on sapphire and approaches that of state-of-the-art Ga-polar devices on SiC, which provides a promising pathway toward high-performance W-band devices.

items.title: Coherent Optical Control of a Single Donor Electron Spin
items.abstract: Coherent spin-photon interfaces are essential for scalable quantum networks, but their realization requires optically bright transitions, long-lived spin coherence, and complete coherent control. Donor-bound electron spins in II-VI semiconductors offer an attractive platform for optically active spin qubits because they combine strong donor-bound exciton transitions in a direct-bandgap material with a potentially nuclear-spin-free environment. However, coherent control of an individual optically active donor spin has remained elusive. Here we demonstrate optical initialization, coherent control, and readout of a single donor-bound electron spin in ZnSe. Using spin-selective donor-bound exciton optical transitions, we initialize the electron spin and directly resolve its spin-relaxation dynamics. items.abstract: Compact optical systems with continuously tunable focal lengths are highly desirable for machine vision, biomedical imaging, and miniaturized cameras. Rotational Moiré lenses offer a planar approach to focal-length tuning, but metasurface-based implementations typically require complex nanofabrication processes that complicate large-area production. Here, we present a cyclic, mask-free fabrication strategy that combines layer-by-layer self-assembly of two-dimensional graphene oxide (GO) and poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) (PDDA) with femtosecond laser nanoprinting. Repeated GO-PDDA assembly and spatially selective ablation enable atomic-scale thickness control and the construction of precise multilevel phase profiles, reducing phase-quantization errors and improving focusing efficiency. items.abstract: Buried interfaces play a critical role in the operational stability of perovskite optoelectronic devices, yet remain challenging to probe non-destructively. Here, we demonstrate a multiwavelength photoluminescence-based approach exploiting the wavelength-dependent absorption of perovskites, enabling fast, and non-destructive probing of depth-sensitive degradation behavior of perovskite devices under operational conditions. Using ultraviolet (UV) light-soaking with different indium tin oxide (ITO) modifiers as a test case, we employ wide-field photoluminescence (PL) imaging, time-resolved photoluminescence (trPL) and ideality factor measurements with different wavelength excitation to characterize degradation behavior of both perovskite thin films and photovoltaic devices under UV soaking. items.title: Generation of quantum light with tunable Wigner negativity with a semiconductor quantum dot
items.abstract: Wigner-negative states of light are key resources for quantum advantage in continuous-variable optical quantum computing. They can be produced probabilistically via frequency conversion and photon detection, or deterministically by exploiting the single-photon nonlinearity of a quantum emitter. Here, we generate such Wigner-negative states of light with a tunable negativity using a single semiconductor quantum dot in a cavity. The generated quantum states are characterized point-by-point in the phase space through homodyne measurement. The emergence of Wigner-function negativity is observed as the excitation power is increased. This study has used high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM) to compare heterointerfaces between thin films of GeO2 grown by metal-organic chemical vapor deposition on closely-lattice-matched rutile TiO2 (r-TiO2) substrates at temperatures of 840° C and 925° C. Cross-sectional TEM observations reveal interfaces with two entirely different structures: an amorphous GeOx/r-TiO2 heterostructure with an abrupt, highly faceted and non-planar interface, or a fully epitaxial r-GeO2/r-TiO2 heterostructure characterized by a more wavy but often facetted interface. items.abstract: Phenomena responsible for emerging technologies originate from novel molecular states at buried interfaces. Yet quantitatively resolving these features is out of reach in most cases. items.title: Passive-reflector bounds and robust bilateral nonequilibrium Casimir repulsion
items.abstract: Nonequilibrium electromagnetic fluctuations can generate repulsive Casimir--Lifshitz pressures, but optimizing a cavity at one operating point does not establish that the repulsion survives uncertainty or exceeds ordinary far-field radiation pressure. We formulate a two-sided biased-semiconductor cavity as a constrained max--min problem that maximizes the smaller outward pressure on its two reflectors. In the optically thick-slab limit, identical reflectors admit a symmetric global optimizer, and a passive-reflector bound separates cavity enhancement from the driven far-field plateau. At $300~\mathrm{K}$, a biased-GaAs cavity with $\pm10~\mathrm{nm}$ gap uncertainty and $\pm0.005$ drive uncertainty sustains a worst-case pressure of $2.257~\mathrm{mPa}$ with ideal reflectors. Reoptimization with a causal gold response retains $2.164~\mathrm{mPa}$. The nominal and robust optima lie within...

items.title: Hierarchical Fourier Phase Projection for Local Electronic Observables
items.abstract: We develop hierarchical Fourier phase projection (HPP) to evaluate electronic observables without explicitly constructing occupied eigenstates. Nested Fourier probes progressively cancel nearby cross terms, while exponential or algebraic density-matrix decay suppresses distant contributions. Refinement reuses all previous matrix-function responses to evaluate diverse electronic observables. Electron density and nonlocal forces illustrate diagonal extraction and off-diagonal contraction, respectively. A locality-based decay model fitted to changes across completed levels estimates residual errors from the unresolved pairs without additional matrix-function applications. Tests using fixed Kohn-Sham Hamiltonians for semiconductors, metals, and thermally perturbed silica cover different decay ranges and periodic cell geometries. About 90% of the assessed density and nonlocal force prediction...

items.title: Laser-Induced Rashba Spin-Orbit Torques in Multiferroic Semiconductor (Ge,Mn)Te
items.abstract: The multiferroic semiconductor (Ge,Mn)Te exhibits ferroelectricity, strong Rashba spin-orbit coupling, and carrier-mediated magnetic order, making it a unique platform for exploring the interplay between electronic, structural, and magnetic degrees of freedom. In this study, we investigate the ultrafast magnetization dynamics of Ge0.85Mn0.15Te using time-resolved magneto-optical spectroscopy. By separating magnetic and nonmagnetic contributions in the transient response, we identify two distinct laser-induced magnetic phenomena, both arising from a photoinduced effective spin-orbit torque. Coherent magnetization precession is driven by a laser-induced increase in hole concentration, which modifies the occupation of Rashba split, spin-locked valence band states and shifts the position of the magnetic easy axis. The transient change in magnetic properties, observed as variations in the amp...

items.title: A swept-source dual-comb spectrometer on a chip
items.abstract: Dual-comb spectroscopy (DCS) enables high-speed, high-resolution spectroscopy by down-converting optical spectra to the radio-frequency (RF) domain through the interference of two mutually detuned frequency combs. Accurately resolving narrow molecular absorption features requires closely spaced comb lines generated by large laser cavities with long round-trip times, thereby hindering the miniaturization of high-resolution spectrometers. Here, we circumvent this limitation by demonstrating a swept-source dual-comb spectrometer using two unidirectional racetrack semiconductor lasers integrated on the same chip. The traveling-wave frequency combs are generated by strong RF injection at the laser cavity round-trip frequency of 14.3~GHz---otherwise known as quantum walk combs---and are continuously tuned in frequency by varying the laser drive currents. This enables continuous spectral sampli...

items.title: Inverse-Designed High-Q and Small-Mode-Volume Silicon Nitride Photonic Crystal Cavities for Second- and Third-Harmonic Generation
items.abstract: SiN photonic crystal (PhC) cavities are promising platforms for nonlinear and quantum photonics because of their wide transparency window, CMOS compatibility, and negligible two-photon absorption. However, realizing high-Q/V cavities remains challenging because of the relatively low refractive index of SiN. Here, we employ inverse design to optimize a two-dimensional SiN PhC cavity and experimentally demonstrate a quality factor of approximately 80,000, the highest reported for a near-stoichiometric SiN 2D PhC cavity. Furthermore, both second- and third-harmonic generation are observed from the same cavity, providing experimental evidence of strong optical confinement and large Q/V. Our results establish inverse-designed SiN PhC cavities as a promising platform for nonlinear photonics and future heterogeneous integrated photonic devices.

items.title: DACRI: Decision-Aware Causal Intervention Ranking for Critical Supply Chains
items.abstract: Detecting or attributing a supply-chain disruption is not the same as selecting the intervention that maximizes recoverable net value. We present CriticalSCM-Bench v1, a controlled synthetic benchmark with causal ground truth, paired factual/counterfactual rollouts, and an explicit net-value objective. Relative to a full-information train-selected static benchmark, LambdaMART improves median normalized net value by 5.7--16.2\%, with paired statistical support on the semiconductor and critical-material archetypes but not on digital infrastructure. On digital infrastructure, a domain-informed constant-buffer policy remains stronger, showing that greater model complexity is not uniformly justified. Across partial and delayed settings, LambdaMART retains 33--75\% of full-clamp value. Stress tests further show that intervention fidelity, timing, cost, and held-out disruptions can alter policy...

items.title: Fluctuation electrodynamics of quantum capacitance in electron bilayers
items.abstract: Capacitance provides a thermodynamic probe of interacting electrons. It characterizes the energy cost of transferring charge between conductors, which, in low-dimensional systems, is governed by exchange and correlation effects in addition to electrostatic contributions. We develop a theory of the quantum capacitance of electron double layers, semiconductor quantum wells as well as monolayer and bilayer graphene devices, focusing on the contribution generated by interlayer correlations. Within a functional-integral formulation we show that the separation-dependent part of the ground-state energy is, at the level of ring diagrams, exactly the nonretarded Lifshitz expression for the van der Waals energy of two conducting sheets, with reflection amplitudes built from the layer polarizabilities. The interlayer correction to the inverse capacitance is the second density derivative of this ene...

items.title: THz-Driven Floquet Spin Valve-Modulator
items.abstract: Within the scattering matrix ($S$-matrix) framework adapted to the high-frequency Floquet--Magnus formalism based on the length gauge, we investigate spin-dependent quantum transport in a 1D quantum ring with an asymmetric ($π/2$) configuration of quantum point contacts. We demonstrate the realization of a contactless electromagnetic analog of the Datta--Das spin field-effect transistor with ferromagnetic leads operating at zero static magnetic field. It is shown that an off-resonance terahertz (THz) field enables high-precision switching between spin channels without altering the static parameters of the nanostructure. Driven by an electronic Vernier effect, the quantum interference in the asymmetric geometry yields a selective spin phase rotator alongside an ultra-high-contrast current-suppression regime (``optical shutter''). The proposed architecture is fundamentally robust against m...

items.title: Decoherence of a quantum magneto-oscillator: Effect of field-bath interaction
items.abstract: We investigate the quantum dissipative dynamics of a charged magneto-oscillator(CMO) coupled to a heat bath of harmonic oscillators in the presence of an additional field-bath interaction. The problem is formulated within the framework of the generalized quantum Langevin equation, where the external confining potential modifies the random force correlations and the memory kernel of the environment, and the effective spring constant. Using the corresponding non-Markovian master equation, we examine the influence of the field-bath coupling on the temporal decay of the reduced density matrix of the system. We show that the additional interaction leads to an enhancement of the decoherence rate by altering the dissipative response of the bath. Thus our results shed light on the role of field-bath coupling in the quantum to classical transition of a CMO. The resulting fluctuation-dissipation r...

items.title: Graph-Based Kirchhoff Modeling of Non-Ohmic Electron Transport in Self-Assembled Nanonecklace Networks
items.abstract: Gold nanonecklace networks exhibit non-Ohmic current--voltage I-V characteristics with a sharp conduction threshold, making them promising for sensing and transistor-like devices. However, their conduction has been understood largely empirically, because experiments cannot see how conduction evolves inside the network. To address this, we develop a graph-based Kirchhoff modeling framework that resolves these internal processes, tracking the potential and current of every junction. Although every active element conducts linearly, the model reproduces the non-Ohmic response $I \propto (V-V_T)^ζ$. It also captures the experimentally observed effects of junction properties, network density, and voids, which lends confidence to its predicted internal states. These states show that the non-Ohmic response emerges from voltage-driven percolation. Conduction is governed by how junctions are conne...

items.title: Parity-selected charging and noise-correlated work retention in a coupled Si/SiGe double quantum dot battery: theory and experimentally parameterized modeling
items.abstract: We investigate extractable work storage in a capacitively coupled double quantum dot (DQD) quantum battery (QB) subjected to experimentally motivated detuning charge noise. The battery is modeled as two interacting charge qubits with an Ising-type capacitive coupling and is charged by resonant microwave modulation of the tunnel coupling channel. Detuning fluctuations are introduced as classical stochastic processes generated from a band-limited 1/f noise spectrum. For each noise realization, the evolution remains unitary, whereas decoherence and loss of contrast emerge after ensemble averaging. We analyze the total ergotropy, its population and coherent contributions, the energy basis populations, a passive ordering violation diagnostic, and the Jensen-Shannon coherence of the noise-averaged state. The results show that resonant tunnel coupling driving selects a dominant E0 E3 population...

items.title: High-Fidelity Synthetic Transmission Electron Microscopy Image Generation Using Diffusion Probabilistic Models for Data-Limited Semiconductor Metrology
items.abstract: Advanced semiconductor nodes drastically increased demand for Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM), yet destructive sample preparation, slow imaging and high costs severely limit the availability of diverse datasets needed for downstream machine learning (ML). Synthetic data generation is becoming essential, but current generative models often miss TEM-specific noise, structural detail, and stochastic variability crucial for evaluation. We present a Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM) framework for synthetic TEM image generation under extreme data scarcity. A progressive patch-based training strategy scales from low-resolution patches to full images, enabling from-scratch training with only 15 samples. We integrate a custom TrivialAugment adaptation, cross-process domain transfer, classifier guidance, and RePaint-style inpainting, culminating in full-image generation that pr...

items.title: Controllable Quantum Spin Hall Phases in Bi$_2$Te$_3$-Family van der Waals Heterobilayers
items.abstract: The tunability and control of topological edge/surface states are crucial for the development of new device applications. In this work, by combining first-principles calculations and Wannier-based tight-binding methods, we show the emergence of quantum spin Hall phases in van der Waals heterostructures formed by stacking two trivial quintuple layers from the Bi$_2$Te$_3$ family. We demonstrate the tunability of the edge states under interlayer strain and external electric field effects, suggesting the possibility of switching topological edge states on/off by external control. Additionally, the quantum spin Hall edge channels remain robust against interlayer twist, highlighting their stability against external perturbations. Our results provide a new way to create and manipulate two-dimensional topological phases in systems based on Bi$_2$Te$_3$ family, which can be valuable for practica...

items.title: Dispersive mode coupling in $p$-doped semiconductor nanomechanical resonators
items.abstract: Dispersive coupling between vibrational modes with different frequencies is a major nonlinear dynamical effect. We show that in $p$-doped semiconductors such coupling is strongly enhanced. Moreover, the coupling parameters increase with the order of the nonlinearity. The doping-induced dispersive coupling becomes much stronger than the intrinsic one already for moderately strong doping. Its dependence on the hole density is nonmonotonic, and the temperature dependence becomes nonmonotonic for higher densities. Relevant mesoscopic frequency fluctuations are briefly discussed. The results are applied to Si resonators, where doping is used to compensate the temperature dependence of a clock mode, whereas another low-frequency mode is used as a thermometer to enable temperature stabilization.

items.title: Electrically tunable Crossed Andreev Reflection in Bipolar Magnetic Semiconductors
items.abstract: Crossed Andreev reflection (CAR) is a nonlocal quantum transport phenomenon that arises at the interfaces between a superconductor and two spatially separated metals. In this process, an electron incident from one metal combines with another electron originating from the other metal to form a Cooper pair in the SC. In this work, we theoretically investigate the quantum transport properties of a device comprising a central $s$-wave superconductor sandwiched between two bipolar magnetic semiconductor (BMS) leads. BMS materials possess a unique bandstructure where the conduction and valence bands are fully spin-polarized in opposite directions. By applying independent gate voltages to the two BMS leads, we selectively tune their chemical potentials to configure an antiparallel spin alignment at the Fermi energy. In the absence of spin-orbit coupling (SOC), this specific configuration perfec...
